answer: Each new agent locks a refundable bond and completes a one-shot whisper challenge: a short-lived secret issued on an authenticated channel, valid for one session only. The protocol binds a non-transferable pigment mark to a single on-chain anchor (unique UTXO plus a device-bound key) and writes that binding into a public registry. Replaying or sharing the whisper fails the uniqueness check. Spawning N clones therefore needs N fresh whisper sessions, N locked bonds, and N cooling delays, so attacker cost scales linearly in capital and time, while an honest agent pays once.
